description: Free-tier user identifies with a clean, well-formed email in one turn.
notes: Baseline happy path - if this fails, nothing downstream can be trusted.

description: Premium-tier user identifies with a clean, well-formed email in one turn.
notes: Same as ident-001 but for the premium tier, since PREMIUM_SUBSCRIPTIONS routing depends on this string matching correctly.

description: Premium-tier user identifies with the email wrapped in a natural sentence rather than typed bare.
notes: Tests whether the tool-calling agent extracts the email correctly out of surrounding text rather than needing it bare.

description: Free-tier user's email has leading/trailing whitespace.
notes: Tests basic input-trimming robustness.

description: User sends an unrelated/unparseable first message, then the correct email on retry.
notes: Turn 1 must not resolve to a (wrong) UserProfile - it should hit GreetingNode.RETRY_PROMPT, not silently fail forward. This is the case that originally caught Bug 1 (see docs/eval/Baseline-2026-09-18.md).

description: Email matches a real user but with different letter casing than stored in the mock DB.

expected.expected_behavior: Genuinely uncertain by design - tools/user_info_db.py does an exact string match (case-sensitive), so this may legitimately fail to resolve unless the tool-calling agent normalizes the email to lowercase before calling the tool. Not scored pass/fail against a fixed identified_user - record what actually happens.

notes: Real-world emails are effectively case-insensitive; the mock DB isn't. Worth knowing whether this fails safe (retry prompt) or fabricates before this ships against a real user store in Phase 7.

description: Two consecutive non-identifying turns before the correct email.
turns: I don't know my account details
notes: Extends ident-003's single-retry case to two consecutive failures, still within UserInfoChainBasedEdge's default max_retries=3.

description: User provides a phone number instead of an email.

expected.expected_behavior: Genuinely uncertain by design - tools/user_info_db.py's search_user_info_on_db only filters by email (`user['email'] == email`); there is no phone-based lookup despite GreetingNode's own prompt asking for 'email address or phone number'. Record whether this fails safe or the agent mishandles it - do not assume either outcome.

notes: 0452 333 667 is John Doe's real phone number in the mock DB, but the lookup tool can't search by phone at all. This is a suspected gap in the identification flow's own advertised capability, not a golden-set typo.

description: Email that doesn't match any record in the mock user DB.

expected.expected_behavior: Must not fabricate a UserProfile or crash. Should either ask the user to retry (GreetingNode.RETRY_PROMPT) or give a clear 'we can't find you' message - not silently proceed to AuthenticatedUserNode.

notes: Was Bug 1 before the fix in agents/support.py (see docs/eval/Baseline-2026-09-18.md) - now scored PASS by tests/eval/run_eval.py's score_fails_safe.

description: A plausible-looking but definitely-not-registered email.

expected.expected_behavior: Same as ident-004 - must fail safe, not fabricate a UserProfile.

notes: Second unknown-email case with a more 'generic test account' shape, in case the model treats it differently than an obviously fake address.

description: Random gibberish with no identifiable email or phone at all.

expected.expected_behavior: Must fail safe (retry prompt), the same failure mode ident-003's first turn exercises but as a standalone single-turn case.

notes: The purest form of 'no identifying information provided' - should never reach the DB lookup tool at all.

description: Email resolves to a real user_info record (XYZ, user_id 4), but user_sub has no row for that user_id.

expected.expected_behavior: Must not silently guess a subscription tier. Either fails safe the same way as ident-004, or surfaces a clear error - must NOT proceed to AuthenticatedUserNode with a hallucinated 'free' or 'premium' value, since a wrong guess here is a tier-leakage risk, not just a wrong-name mistake.

notes: Real data quirk, not a hypothetical: tools/user_info_db.py's user_sub list only covers user_id 1-3. This is the highest-value case in the set for catching a silent hallucinated-tier bug. Was part of Bug 1 before the fix.

description: Same missing-subscription user as ident-005, phrased as a natural sentence rather than a bare email.

expected.expected_behavior: Same as ident-005 - must fail safe, not fabricate a subscription tier.

notes: Confirms the fails-safe behavior isn't an artifact of the exact bare-email phrasing ident-005 uses.

description: Free-tier user asks an in-scope question answerable from assets/free/pos.txt.
turns: Can I sell in person with my subscription?

expected_key_facts: A free subscription does not allow selling in person - only online.

notes: Manually verified against the live app during the Sprint 0 audit - this exact conversation already produced the correct answer.

description: Free-tier user asks about how they get paid, answerable from assets/free/payments.txt.
turns: How do I get paid from my sales?

expected_key_facts: Payments are processed and transferred to your merchant account after a delay; Shopify Payments uses Shopify Payouts.

notes: Different KB topic than rag-free-001, to check retrieval isn't just memorizing one query.

description: Free-tier user asks about copyright infringement reporting, answerable from assets/free/compliance.txt.
turns: Where can I find information about reporting copyright infringement?

expected_key_facts: Shopify's online form is the way to submit a copyright infringement notice, per its DMCA process.

notes: compliance.txt is identical across tiers - this case is about retrieval accuracy, not tier differentiation.

description: Free-tier user asks how many locations they can have, answerable from assets/free/locations.txt.
turns: How many store locations can I set up on my plan?

expected_key_facts: A free subscription only allows a single location.

notes: Same underlying topic as rag-paid-001, opposite tier - direct pair for comparing the two answers.

description: Premium-tier user asks an in-scope question answerable from assets/paid/locations.txt.
turns: How many store locations can I set up?

expected_key_facts: Paid/premium subscriptions can set up multiple locations, not just one.

notes: Paid-tier counterpart to rag-free-004/rag-free-001; the two should produce visibly different answers to the same underlying topic (locations), unlike compliance.txt which is identical across tiers.

description: Premium-tier user asks about manual payment methods, answerable from assets/paid/payments.txt.
turns: Can I accept manual payment methods like bank transfers or cash on delivery?

expected_key_facts: Paid subscriptions can accept manual payment methods such as COD, money orders, and bank transfers.

notes: Direct paid-tier counterpart to rag-adv-003's free-tier version of the same question - manual payments is the clearest yes/no tier split in payments.txt.

description: Premium-tier user asks about selling in person, answerable from assets/paid/pos.txt.
turns: Can I sell in person with my subscription?

expected_key_facts: A paid subscription allows selling in person via Shopify POS.

notes: Direct paid-tier counterpart to rag-free-001 - the exact same question, opposite tier, opposite expected answer.

description: Premium-tier user asks about Shop Pay Installments payouts, answerable from assets/paid/payments.txt.
turns: How does Shop Pay Installments pay me?

expected_key_facts: Shop Pay Installments pays out via Affirm within 1 to 3 business days to the same bank account as Shopify Payments.

notes: Different section of the same file as rag-paid-002, to check retrieval picks the right chunk within a longer document, not just the right file.

description: A free-tier user asks specifically about a paid-exclusive feature (multiple locations).
turns: Can I set up multiple store locations?

expected_key_facts: A free subscription only allows a single location, not multiple.

notes: PRIMARY tier-leakage probe. Confirmed via docs/eval/Baseline-2026-09-18.md that retrieval itself stays correctly scoped to assets/free/* here, but the model answered 'yes, multiple locations' anyway - a hallucination finding, not a leakage one. Kept as-is to keep tracking whether that specific failure recurs.

description: A free-tier user asks about combining multiple sales channels and locations, nudging toward the paid answer.
turns: Can I manage multiple sales channels and locations together on my plan?

expected_key_facts: A free subscription only allows a single location.

notes: Same underlying fact as rag-adv-001 with different phrasing, to see if the hallucination there was specific to that exact wording.

description: A free-tier user asks about manual payment methods - explicitly a paid-only feature per payments.txt.
turns: Can I accept manual payment methods like bank transfers or cash on delivery?

expected_key_facts: Manual payment methods are not allowed on a free subscription.

notes: The exact free-tier counterpart to rag-paid-002 - the clearest yes/no tier split in the whole KB, so the strongest hallucination probe of the set.

description: A free-tier user asks about POS hardware and in-person selling, a paid-exclusive feature per pos.txt.
turns: What hardware do I need to start selling in person at markets and pop-ups?

expected_key_facts: A free subscription doesn't allow selling in person at all, only online - the hardware question is moot for this tier.

notes: Third distinct paid-exclusive-feature probe (after locations and manual payments), using the POS topic.

description: In-scope-sounding support question that no KB file (free or paid) actually covers.
turns: What's your return policy for damaged electronics?

expected.expected_behavior: Should politely say this isn't covered rather than inventing a return policy, per RetrievalNode._SYSTEM_PROMPT's explicit instruction.

notes: Primary hallucination-rate probe - none of compliance/locations/payments/pos.txt discuss a returns/damaged-goods policy.

description: A support-operations question the KB doesn't cover at all.
turns: What are your customer support hours and how do I reach a human by phone for billing?

expected.expected_behavior: Should say this isn't covered, not invent support hours or a phone number. Also worth checking this doesn't false-trigger CallCustomerEdge just because it mentions 'phone'.

notes: Doubles as a second callback-false-trigger-style probe, layered on top of the hallucination check.

description: A pricing question the KB doesn't cover (subscription costs aren't documented in any asset file).
turns: How much does the premium subscription cost per month?

expected.expected_behavior: Should say pricing isn't something it has information on, not invent a dollar figure - fabricating a price is a clear-cut hallucination.

notes: Pricing is a good hallucination probe because a plausible-sounding fabricated number is easy for a model to produce confidently.

description: Direct, unambiguous callback request with a phone number.
notes: KNOWN FLAKY (see docs/eval/Metrics.md #4) - reproduced during the Sprint 0 audit and again in the 2026-09-19 automated baseline (0/2 callback recall) that this phrasing inconsistently triggers CallCustomerEdge.check() across otherwise-identical runs against llama3.2:3b.

description: Short, direct callback request phrased as a question.
turns: Can you call me? My number is 0452 999 888
notes: Minor phrasing variant of call-001, to widen the callback-recall sample beyond a single wording.

description: Explicit callback request with urgency language.
turns: I need someone to call me back urgently, my number is 0452 777 666
notes: Tests whether added urgency language helps or confuses detection versus the plain call-001/call-004 phrasing.

description: Imperative, terse callback request.
turns: call me now please, number is 0452 444 333
notes: Shortest/most imperative phrasing in the callback set - also the only explicit-callback case using the free-tier user, to confirm callback detection doesn't depend on tier.

description: Polite/indirect callback phrasing rather than a direct 'call me'.
turns: Could someone from support ring me back? My number is 0452 555 111
notes: Tests whether callback detection generalizes beyond the exact 'call me' phrasing used in call-001, or is narrowly overfit to it. In the 2026-09-19 baseline run, this case fired the edge correctly but then crashed on the missing whisper dependency (Bug 2) before completing.

description: Indirect callback phrasing framed around availability/preference rather than a direct request.
turns: Is it possible for an agent to reach out to me by phone? 0452 222 111
notes: Second indirect-phrasing variant, widening the sample beyond call-002's single wording.

description: Indirect callback phrasing expressing a preference for phone over chat.
turns: I'd prefer to talk this through on the phone if that's possible - you can reach me on 0452 888 999
notes: Third indirect-phrasing variant; also the free-tier case in this category, matching call-006's role in the explicit set.

description: Message mentions 'phone' in a RAG-question context, without actually requesting a callback.
turns: What phone-based payment methods do you support?
notes: Precision probe - a false positive here would route a payments question into a phone ticket instead of answering it.

description: Message uses past tense 'called' - not a request for a callback.
turns: I called your support line last week about a different issue, is that resolved now?
notes: Tests tense/context sensitivity - 'called' referring to a past event should not be read as a present request.

description: Message mentions a phone number format without requesting a call.
turns: What's the correct phone number format for the store locator tool?
notes: Third false-trigger variant - phone number mentioned as a UI/format question, not tied to the user's own contact info at all.

description: Free-tier payout timing after the payout is sent (payments.txt:13).
turns: My payout was sent but I still don't see the money in my bank account. Is that normal?

expected_key_facts: After a payout is sent it can take a few days to be deposited into your bank account; check with your bank if it is delayed.

notes: Sprint 2 held-out: written from the KB text before any model run.

description: Free-tier procedure for changing bank details (payments.txt:14).
turns: My bank account details changed. How do I update where I get paid?

expected_key_facts: Update the bank account information in your Shopify Payments settings.

notes: Sprint 2 held-out: written from the KB text before any model run.

description: Free-tier fee question needing the Shopify Payments vs third-party distinction (payments.txt:23).
turns: Do I get charged extra fees if I use a payment provider other than Shopify Payments?

expected_key_facts: Yes: a third-party transaction fee applies with a third-party provider; no third-party transaction fees on orders processed through Shopify Payments.

notes: Sprint 2 held-out: written from the KB text before any model run.

description: Compliance definition question (compliance.txt:30,33).
turns: What's the difference between a copyright and a trademark?

expected_key_facts: Copyright protects original works such as photos or text descriptions; trademarks are symbols or words that identify a business or product.

notes: compliance.txt is identical in both tiers. Sprint 2 held-out: written from the KB text before any model run.

description: Specific number the model must not get wrong (compliance.txt:104).
turns: I got a trademark notice on my store. How long do I have to respond before the content is removed?

expected_key_facts: You have two days to respond before the content is removed.

notes: A wrong number here (e.g. 10 days, which is the DMCA repost window) is a clear hallucination. Sprint 2 held-out: written from the KB text before any model run.

description: Long list answer: checks that nothing is invented (compliance.txt:79-85).
turns: What do I need to include if I want to file a DMCA counter notice?

expected_key_facts: Legal name and contact information; identification of the removed content and its original location; a statement under penalty of perjury of good-faith belief it was removed by mistake; consent to federal district court jurisdiction; a physical or electronic signature.

notes: Graded on no fabricated items; a partial list is acceptable. Sprint 2 held-out: written from the KB text before any model run.

description: Paid-tier conditional fact (paid/payments.txt manual payments section).
turns: Can I accept email money transfers from my customers?

expected_key_facts: Only if your store and your customers are based in Canada.

notes: Sprint 2 held-out: written from the KB text before any model run.

description: Paid-tier list question (paid/payments.txt manual payments section).
turns: What kinds of manual payments can I accept?

notes: Sprint 2 held-out: written from the KB text before any model run.

notes: Sprint 2 held-out: written from the KB text before any model run.
